item.title: Nadi move to top of Skipper Cup Senior points table
item.description: Nadi have moved to the top of the Skipper Cup Senior points table after seven rounds, remaining unbeaten as the competition enters its crucial stages. Nadi have recorded six wins and one draw from seven matches to collect 30 points.
item.content:encoded:
Nadi have moved to the top of the Skipper Cup Senior points table after seven rounds, remaining unbeaten as the competition enters its crucial stages.

Nadi have recorded six wins and one draw from seven matches to collect 30 points.

They also have a points differential of +70, underlining their consistency throughout the opening seven rounds.

Nadi are level on 30 points with Tailevu, who have five wins and two draws, but Nadi sit at the top of the table due to their superior points differential.

Nadroga and Naitasiri are next on 27 points, with Nadroga recording five wins, one draw and one loss, along with an impressive points differential of +108.

Naitasiri have recorded five wins and two losses.

Defending champions Malolo are fifth with 23 points, followed by Suva on 20 points.

Further down the table, Navosa have 17 points, while Taveuni are on 14 points.

Ba are on 13 points, while Lautoka and Kadavu have 10 points each.

Rewa remain at the bottom of the table with eight points.

With the competition moving towards its decisive rounds, Nadi will be looking to maintain their unbeaten run and stay at the top as the battle for the leading positions intensifies.

item.title: Flying Fijians eye strong finish against Japan
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians scrum-half Sam Wye is anticipating a tough battle against hosts Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final this Saturday. Speaking from Japan during a training session, Wye says the players are excited to be in their third consecutive final and hope to finish the tournament strongly this week.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians scrum-half Sam Wye is anticipating a tough battle against hosts Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final this Saturday.

Speaking from Japan during a training session, Wye says the players are excited to be in their third consecutive final and hope to finish the tournament strongly this week.

Wye says they are aware of the capabilities of the Japanese team.

He says the players are happy in camp and are looking forward to another final this Saturday.

Fiji will face Japan this Saturday at 7.05pm.

In the other match, Canada will play the United States of America for third place.

item.title: Fiji Pearls edge Cook Islands 65-63 in Oceania qualifiers opener
item.description: The Crest Fiji Pearls have won their first game at the Oceania Netball World Cup qualifiers edging the Cook Islands 65-63. The lead went back and forth between the two sides with Cook Islands leading 36-32 at half time.
item.content:encoded:
The Crest Fiji Pearls have won their first game at the Oceania Netball World Cup qualifiers edging the Cook Islands 65-63.

The lead went back and forth between the two sides with Cook Islands leading 36-32 at half time.

The Fiji Pearls fought back in the final quarter to take the game.

They will now face Samoa at 3pm tomorrow.

The Fiji Pearls will then play hosts Tonga at 3pm Thursday, with their final game against Papua New Guinea at 3pm Friday.

Only the top two teams from the Qualifiers will make it through to the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.

item.title: Ba FC President dedicates Ba’s historic treble to loyal supporters
item.description: Dayal’s Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal has dedicated the team’s historic 2026 treble to the people of Ba and its loyal supporters. Ba won the BiC Fiji FACT, Extra Premier League and Extra Battle of the Giants titles this season, while the team has also qualified for next year’s OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the league.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal’s Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal has dedicated the team’s historic 2026 treble to the people of Ba and its loyal supporters.

Ba won the BiC Fiji FACT, Extra Premier League and Extra Battle of the Giants titles this season, while the team has also qualified for next year’s OFC Men’s Champions League after winning the league.

Dayal says the success belongs to every Ba supporter who continued to believe in the team.

He says the achievement follows a promise he made to supporters after Ba lost to Rewa in last year’s Inter-District Championship final.

Dayal says seeing supporters leave the stadium heartbroken after the defeat strengthened his determination to restore Ba’s glory days.

He says the team remained firm through difficult decisions and challenges, supported by the prayers of thousands of supporters.

Dayal says the three trophies now sit proudly in Ba’s cabinet and the team will represent Ba and Fiji at the regional level next year.

He says the success belongs not only to the board, coaching staff and players, but also to the supporters who stood by the team throughout the season.

item.title: Seta Tamanivalu called in as injury cover for Ravouvou
item.description: Former All Blacks centre Setareki Tamanivalu has been called into the FIJI Water Flying Fijians squad ahead of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final against hosts Japan on Saturday. Tamanivalu has been called in as cover for Kalaveti Ravouvou who has been ruled out of this weekend's game due to injury.
item.content:encoded:
Former All Blacks centre Setareki Tamanivalu has been called into the FIJI Water Flying Fijians squad ahead of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final against hosts Japan on Saturday.

Tamanivalu has been called in as cover for Kalaveti Ravouvou who has been ruled out of this weekend's game due to injury.

The Flying Fijians are currently riding on a high after besting 24th placed Canada 45-29 in an electric semi-final.

Interim Coach Senirusi Seruvakula says they will be looking to build on the positives from their win over Canada.

Seruvakula says Fiji will be aiming to maintain their winning momentum and put themselves in a strong position as they battle for top honours in the Pacific Nations Cup.

Japan are expected to provide a different challenge, with their pace, discipline and attacking style likely to test Fiji across the field.

The Flying Fijians will face Japan at 7.05pm Saturday.

item.description: Fiji Netball has confirmed that the Pearls enjoyed a positive final session, with the players showing plenty of energy and enthusiasm as they put the finishing touches to their preparations. They say the players are ready for a match that could set the tone for their campaign in Tonga.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Netball has confirmed that the Pearls enjoyed a positive final session, with the players showing plenty of energy and enthusiasm as they put the finishing touches to their preparations.

They say the players are ready for a match that could set the tone for their campaign in Tonga.

Fiji's preparations have been built around taking the tournament one match at a time, with head coach Michelle Parsons stressing the importance of treating every game like a final.

Parsons says the team knows there is little room for error in a five-day qualifying tournament featuring Fiji, the Cook Islands, Tonga, Samoa and Papua New Guinea.

The players' high spirits will be welcomed by the coaching staff, but the real test begins when the first whistle sounds.

The Fiji Pearls will face the Cook Islands today at 5pm.
